```text
## Description

Adds bulk actions to the Schedules page (#65). Before this change, schedules could only be changed one at a time through each row's "⋯" menu, unlike Rules, Payees, Tags and Transactions, which all let you tick rows and act on them together.

- **`SchedulesTable.tsx`:**
  - Each active schedule row has a checkbox, shown on hover or when the row is selected, and the header has a select-all checkbox. Selected rows are highlighted the same way as on the Rules and Tags pages.
  - Completed rows get an empty space in place of the checkbox, so the columns stay aligned.
  - Clicking a row still opens the schedule editor. Clicking the checkbox only changes the selection.
  - The compact table used by the schedule picker on transactions (`ScheduleLink`) has no checkboxes and is unchanged.
- **`SelectedSchedulesButton.tsx` (new):** an "N schedules" dropdown next to the search box, built on the shared `SelectedItemsButton`. It offers the same actions as a row's menu: Post transaction, Post transaction today, Skip next scheduled date, Complete and Delete. Restart is left out because it only applies to completed schedules.
- **`index.tsx`:**
  - The page is wrapped in a `SelectedProvider`. Only schedules that are visible and not completed can be selected.
  - The action handling moved into a shared `runScheduleAction` function, used by both the row menu and the bulk button.
- **`useFilteredSchedules.ts` (new):** the search filter moved out of `SchedulesTable` so the page and the table work from the same filtered list.
- **E2E:** new page-model helpers, plus tests for bulk skip, complete and delete, completed rows having no checkbox, select-all, and row click still opening the editor.

## Design Decisions

- **Bulk actions run in a loop on the client, calling the existing single-schedule action once per selected schedule.** This reuses the server methods the row menu already calls, so the behaviour of each action is unchanged and no `loot-core` code changes. One alternative was considered:
  1. **Edit all selected schedules at once with batch server methods** (e.g. `schedule/delete-all`, following the existing `rule-delete-all`).
     - Pros: one request per bulk action instead of one per schedule, the data refreshes once, and a single undo reverts the whole bulk action.
     - Cons: needs four new server methods with types and tests. Posting a transaction and skipping a date each run per-schedule logic (rules, next-date calculation) that would have to be restructured to run in a batch.
     - Status: left as a follow-up if undoing one schedule at a time proves to be a problem.
- **Completed schedules have no checkbox.** The issue says completed schedules can't be bulk-edited, and leaving out the checkbox enforces that without extra rules in the menu. One alternative was considered:
  1. **Let completed schedules be selected, and disable or hide the actions that don't apply to them**, offering Restart when only completed schedules are selected.
     - Pros: would also allow bulk restarting or deleting completed schedules.
     - Cons: editing completed schedules is out of scope for the issue. Mixed selections would need rules for which actions to show, and select-all would have to decide whether to include completed schedules hidden behind "Show completed schedules".
     - Status: not done.
- **Only visible, active schedules can be selected.** The selection is given only the schedules matching the search filter that aren't completed. Select-all and shift-click therefore never pick up hidden or completed schedules. A schedule that is completed or deleted also drops out of the selection on its own.
- **The bulk button sits in the top bar next to the search box**, matching the Tags, Rules and Payees pages.
- **Clicking a row still opens the editor.** The checkbox stops the click from reaching the row, as it does on the Rules page.
- **The selection is kept after Post and Skip, and cleared after Complete and Delete.** Posting or skipping can sensibly be repeated on the same schedules, while completed and deleted schedules can no longer be selected.
- **No keyboard shortcuts**, since the issue lists them as out of scope.

## Tech Debt

**Introduced**
- Each schedule in a bulk action is its own undo step, so undoing a bulk delete of five schedules takes five undos.
- If one schedule's action fails partway through a bulk action, the loop stops. Schedules before it have already been changed, and no error is shown, the same as when a single-row action fails today.
- The search filter now runs twice per render, once in the page to work out what can be selected and once in the table to show rows. Both use the same hook, so the results match.
- The action labels are written out in both the row menu and the bulk button.
- The new checkbox column changes the Schedules page screenshots, so the visual regression snapshots need regenerating.

**Encountered**
- Row checkboxes are revealed on hover, which redraws the cell when the pointer enters the row. In tests, a click that doesn't hover first is lost. The Tags and Rules tables reveal their checkboxes the same way. The new tests hover before clicking.
- The schedule edit modal's `add()` page-model helper doesn't wait for the modal to close, so tests that click the table right after adding a schedule have to wait for it themselves.
- `SchedulesTable.tsx` is still excluded from strict type checking (`@ts-strict-ignore`).

## Related issue(s)

Closes #65
```

```text
+    await expect(appleRow.getByTestId('date')).toHaveText('02/01/2017');

+    await schedulesPage.performBulkAction('Complete');
+    await expect(selectButton).toHaveCount(0);
+    await expect(rows.last()).toHaveText('Show completed schedules');
+
+    // Completed schedules have no checkbox and are skipped by select-all

+
+    await schedulesPage.toggleSelectAll();

+
+    // Deletes the four active schedules, leaving the completed ones

+    await expect(selectButton).toHaveCount(0);

+    await expect(homeDepotRow).toHaveCount(1);

diff --git a/packages/desktop-client/src/components/schedules/SelectedSchedulesButton.tsx b/packages/desktop-client/src/components/schedules/SelectedSchedulesButton.tsx
new file mode 100644
index 000000000..d72e76014
--- /dev/null
+++ b/packages/desktop-client/src/components/schedules/SelectedSchedulesButton.tsx
@@ -0,0 +1,50 @@
+import { useTranslation } from 'react-i18next';
+
+import type { ScheduleEntity } from '@actual-app/core/types/models';
+
+import { SelectedItemsButton } from '#components/table';
+import { useSelectedDispatch } from '#hooks/useSelected';
+
+import type { ScheduleItemAction } from './SchedulesTable';
+
+// Restart only applies to completed schedules, which can't be selected
+type Actions = Exclude<ScheduleItemAction, 'restart'>;
+
+type SelectedSchedulesButtonProps = {
+  onAction: (name: Actions, id: ScheduleEntity['id']) => Promise<void>;
+};
+
+export function SelectedSchedulesButton({
+  onAction,
+}: SelectedSchedulesButtonProps) {
+  const { t } = useTranslation();
+  const dispatch = useSelectedDispatch();
+
+  async function handleSelect(name: Actions, scheduleIds: string[]) {
+    for (const id of scheduleIds) {
+      await onAction(name, id);
+    }
+
+    // Completed and deleted schedules leave the selectable list
+    if (name === 'complete' || name === 'delete') {
+      dispatch({ type: 'select-none' });
+    }
+  }
+
+  return (
+    <SelectedItemsButton<Actions>
+      id="selected-schedules"
+      name={count =>
+        count === 1 ? t('1 schedule') : t('{{count}} schedules', { count })
+      }
+      items={[
+        { name: 'post-transaction', text: t('Post transaction') },
+        { name: 'post-transaction-today', text: t('Post transaction today') },
+        { name: 'skip', text: t('Skip next scheduled date') },
+        { name: 'complete', text: t('Complete') },
+        { name: 'delete', text: t('Delete') },
+      ]}
+      onSelect={(name, ids) => void handleSelect(name, ids)}
+    />
+  );
+}

+async function runScheduleAction(

+) {
+  switch (name) {
+    case 'post-transaction':
+      await send('schedule/post-transaction', { id });
+      break;
+    case 'post-transaction-today':
+      await send('schedule/post-transaction', { id, today: true });
+      break;
+    case 'skip':
+      await send('schedule/skip-next-date', { id });
+      break;
+    case 'complete':
+      await send('schedule/update', {
+        schedule: { id, completed: true },
+      });
+      break;
+    case 'restart':
+      await send('schedule/update', {
+        schedule: { id, completed: false },
+        resetNextDate: true,
+      });
+      break;
+    case 'delete':
+      await send('schedule/delete', { id });
+      break;
+    default:
+      throw new Error(`Unknown action: ${String(name)}`);
+  }
+}

new file mode 100644
index 000000000..ddd14a801
--- /dev/null
+++ b/packages/desktop-client/src/components/schedules/useFilteredSchedules.ts
@@ -0,0 +1,66 @@
+import { useMemo } from 'react';
+
+import { format as monthUtilFormat } from '@actual-app/core/shared/months';
+import { getNormalisedString } from '@actual-app/core/shared/normalisation';
+import { getScheduledAmount } from '@actual-app/core/shared/schedules';
+import type { ScheduleStatuses } from '@actual-app/core/shared/schedules';
+import type { ScheduleEntity } from '@actual-app/core/types/models';
+
+import { useAccounts } from '#hooks/useAccounts';
+import { useDateFormat } from '#hooks/useDateFormat';
+import { useFormat } from '#hooks/useFormat';
+import { usePayees } from '#hooks/usePayees';
+
+type UseFilteredSchedulesProps = {
+  schedules: readonly ScheduleEntity[];
+  filter: string;
+  statuses: ScheduleStatuses;
+};
+
+export function useFilteredSchedules({
+  schedules,
+  filter,
+  statuses,
+}: UseFilteredSchedulesProps): readonly ScheduleEntity[] {
+  const format = useFormat();
+  const dateFormat = useDateFormat() || 'MM/dd/yyyy';
+  const { data: payees = [] } = usePayees();
+  const { data: accounts = [] } = useAccounts();
+
+  return useMemo(() => {
+    if (!filter) {
+      return schedules;
+    }
+    const filterIncludes = (str: string | null | undefined) =>
+      str
+        ? getNormalisedString(str).includes(getNormalisedString(filter)) ||
+          getNormalisedString(filter).includes(getNormalisedString(str))
+        : false;
+
+    return schedules.filter(schedule => {
+      const payee = payees.find(p => schedule._payee === p.id);
+      const account = accounts.find(a => schedule._account === a.id);
+      const amount = getScheduledAmount(schedule._amount);
+      let amountStr = '';
+      if (schedule._amountOp === 'isbetween') {
+        amountStr = '±';
+      } else if (schedule._amountOp === 'isapprox') {
+        amountStr = '~';
+      }
+      amountStr +=
+        (amount > 0 ? '+' : '') + format(Math.abs(amount || 0), 'financial');
+      const dateStr = schedule.next_date
+        ? monthUtilFormat(schedule.next_date, dateFormat)
+        : null;
+
+      return (
+        filterIncludes(schedule.name) ||
+        filterIncludes(payee && payee.name) ||
+        filterIncludes(account && account.name) ||
+        filterIncludes(amountStr) ||
+        filterIncludes(statuses.get(schedule.id)) ||
+        filterIncludes(dateStr)
+      );
+    });
+  }, [payees, accounts, schedules, filter, statuses, format, dateFormat]);
+}
```

```markdown
# Review: PR #129 — [AI] Bulk edit schedules

It reuses `useSelected` and `SelectedItemsButton` the way Rules and Tags do. **But it breaks an existing flow.** The pre-existing e2e test `creates two new schedules, posts both transactions and later completes one` (`schedules.test.ts:181`) times out at line 218 on the first run and on the retry. The CI screenshot shows the row's ⋯ button pressed, but its menu never opens. Functional shard 3 passes on every other open PR, so this PR causes the failure. The likely cause is the new `hovered` state on `ScheduleRow`: it re-renders the row on `mouseenter`, which is the same "lost click" the PR's Tech Debt section describes for the checkboxes. If that's right, real users could see the ⋯ menu fail to open too, so it's more than a test problem. Smaller issue: `onSelect={(name, ids) => void handleSelect(name, ids)}` drops rejections, so a failure partway through a bulk action is silent. |
| Test coverage — are tests present and meaningful? | 6 | The new e2e test is good. It covers selecting without opening the editor, the "1 / 2 schedules" label, skip keeping the selection, complete clearing it, completed rows having no checkbox, select-all skipping completed rows, and bulk delete. A separate test confirms that clicking a row still opens the editor. Gaps: there's no bulk **Post transaction** test, nothing covers shift-click range selection or selection combined with the search filter, an existing test now fails (see above), and the VRT snapshots weren't regenerated, so Visual regression shard 3 fails. |
| Code quality — consistent style, clear naming, no unnecessary duplication | 7 | Mostly clean and follows the codebase's conventions. Pulling the filter out into `useFilteredSchedules` and moving `runScheduleAction` to module scope are good refactors. The `Field width={20}` spacer for completed rows keeps the columns aligned. Issues: (1) `.github/workflows/temp-update-vrt.yml` is committed in a commit titled "Regenerate VRT snapshots". It only triggers on pushes to `fix/update-vrt-snapshots`, so it never ran for this branch, and it's marked TEMPORARY with write permission to push commits. It should come out of this PR. (2) The action labels are duplicated between the row menu and `SelectedSchedulesButton` (already listed as tech debt). (3) The filter runs twice per render. Acknowledged, but the page could pass `filteredSchedules` down to the table instead. |
| Documentation — inline comments and PR description are clear | 7 | The PR description is very thorough. The design decisions, alternatives and tech-debt list are honest and useful. The inline comments are short and explain *why* (e.g. "Completed schedules can't be bulk edited, so they get no checkbox"). Missing: the **UML Diagram** and **Testing** sections are empty, the commit messages don't use the `[AI]` prefix the repo requires, and the "Regenerate VRT snapshots" commit message doesn't match what the commit does. The release note is fine. |
| AI transparency — if AI was used, is there evidence of human verification? | 4 | The `[AI]` prefix on the PR title shows AI was used. There's no sprint 2 AI log for this work under `ai-logs/sprint2/jamesleonard3rd/`, the commits aren't `[AI]`-prefixed, the Testing section is blank and every checklist box (including self-review) is unchecked. The failing CI was pushed without comment, which suggests the change wasn't run and checked by a human before review was requested. |
| Overall — would you merge this as-is? | 5 | **No, request changes.** The design is solid and close to mergeable. Before merging: (1) fix the ⋯-menu regression so `schedules.test.ts:181` passes, by checking whether the hover re-render is the cause, e.g. reveal the checkbox with CSS `:hover` instead of React state; (2) remove `temp-update-vrt.yml` and regenerate the VRT snapshots with `/update-vrt`; (3) add a bulk Post transaction test; (4) fill in Testing and the UML diagram, add the AI log, and complete the checklist. |
```

````markdown
| Correctness — does the change do what the issue asked? | 6 | The feature does what #65 asks: row checkboxes, select-all, an "N schedules" menu with Post / Post today / Skip / Complete / Delete, and completed schedules can't be selected. It reuses `useSelected` and `SelectedItemsButton` the way Rules and Tags do. **But it breaks an existing flow.** The pre-existing e2e test `creates two new schedules, posts both transactions and later completes one` (`schedules.test.ts:181`) times out at line 218 on the first run and on the retry. The CI screenshot shows the row's ⋯ button pressed, but its menu never opens. Functional shard 3 passes on every other open PR, so this PR causes the failure. The likely cause is the new `hovered` state on `ScheduleRow`: it re-renders the row on `mouseenter`, which is the same "lost click" the PR's Tech Debt section describes for the checkboxes. If that's right, real users could see the ⋯ menu fail to open too, so it's more than a test problem. Smaller issue: `onSelect={(name, ids) => void handleSelect(name, ids)}` drops rejections, so a failure partway through a bulk action is silent. |
| Test coverage — are tests present and meaningful? | 6 | The new e2e test is good. It covers selecting without opening the editor, the "1 / 2 schedules" label, skip keeping the selection, complete clearing it, completed rows having no checkbox, select-all skipping completed rows, and bulk delete. A separate test confirms that clicking a row still opens the editor. Gaps: there's no bulk **Post transaction** test, nothing covers shift-click range selection or selection combined with the search filter, an existing test now fails (see above), and the VRT snapshots weren't regenerated, so Visual regression shard 3 fails. |
| Code quality — consistent style, clear naming, no unnecessary duplication | 7 | Mostly clean and follows the codebase's conventions. Pulling the filter out into `useFilteredSchedules` and moving `runScheduleAction` to module scope are good refactors. The `Field width={20}` spacer for completed rows keeps the columns aligned. Issues: (1) `.github/workflows/temp-update-vrt.yml` is committed in a commit titled "Regenerate VRT snapshots". It only triggers on pushes to `fix/update-vrt-snapshots`, so it never ran for this branch, and it's marked TEMPORARY with write permission to push commits. It should come out of this PR. (2) The action labels are duplicated between the row menu and `SelectedSchedulesButton` (already listed as tech debt). (3) The filter runs twice per render. Acknowledged, but the page could pass `filteredSchedules` down to the table instead. |
| Documentation — inline comments and PR description are clear | 7 | The PR description is very thorough. The design decisions, alternatives and tech-debt list are honest and useful. The inline comments are short and explain _why_ (e.g. "Completed schedules can't be bulk edited, so they get no checkbox"). Missing: the **UML Diagram** and **Testing** sections are empty, the commit messages don't use the `[AI]` prefix the repo requires, and the "Regenerate VRT snapshots" commit message doesn't match what the commit does. The release note is fine. |
| AI transparency — if AI was used, is there evidence of human verification? | 4 | The `[AI]` prefix on the PR title shows AI was used. There's no sprint 2 AI log for this work under `ai-logs/sprint2/jamesleonard3rd/`, the commits aren't `[AI]`-prefixed, the Testing section is blank and every checklist box (including self-review) is unchecked. The failing CI was pushed without comment, which suggests the change wasn't run and checked by a human before review was requested. |
| Overall — would you merge this as-is? | 5 | **No, request changes.** The design is solid and close to mergeable. Before merging: (1) fix the ⋯-menu regression so `schedules.test.ts:181` passes, by checking whether the hover re-render is the cause, e.g. reveal the checkbox with CSS `:hover` instead of React state; (2) remove `temp-update-vrt.yml` and regenerate the VRT snapshots with `/update-vrt`; (3) add a bulk Post transaction test; (4) fill in Testing and the UML diagram, add the AI log, and complete the checklist. |

## Evidence

- CI run [40759753284](https://github.com/CSCI-435-SE/actual-budget/actions/runs/40759753284): Functional shard 3/3 and Visual regression shard 3/3 fail; all other checks (typecheck, lint, unit tests, knip) pass.
- Failing step: `await schedulesPage.postNthSchedule(3)` → `waiting for getByRole('button', { name: 'Post transaction today' })` → 60s timeout, on both attempts.
- The new bulk-action tests themselves pass in CI.
````

The cause of the broken test (the hover state) is my best guess from the CI screenshot. I haven't confirmed it by running the tests locally.

# Committing Changes in actualbudget/actual

Before creating any git commit or pull request in this repo, read:

**`.github/agents/pr-and-commit-rules.md`**

It is the authoritative source for the rules you must apply yourself: the `[AI]` PR-title prefix and leaving the PR template blank (and the Chinese exception). The mechanical commit/git rules are enforced by tooling and aren't restated there. Read it on every commit/PR session so any updates are picked up automatically.

## The one rule worth restating

Every commit message and every pull request title MUST begin with `[AI]`. Commit messages are checked by the git-guard hook (a missing prefix is blocked before the commit lands), so the one that needs _your_ attention is the PR title — nothing checks it for you, and the cost of forgetting it is high since the PR has to be renamed by hand. Examples:

- `[AI] Fix type error in account validation` — correct
- `Fix type error in account validation` — wrong, missing prefix

The PR-template rule and the rest live in the rules file. Read it before each commit/PR rather than relying on this skill's summary, because the rules file evolves and this skill deliberately does not restate it.

## Why this matters

Maintainers triage AI-authored contributions separately, and the `[AI]` prefix is what makes that triage fast — it also drives the automatic `"AI generated"` PR label, so getting the prefix right is the one action that gates the whole triage path. Without it the PR looks like a normal human contribution and the wrong review process gets applied. The "do not fill in the PR template" rule exists because the human is the one who actually tested the change and can write the Description / Testing / Checklist sections honestly — an AI-filled template misrepresents who did what.

The rules file is short. Read it.
